findings.where: First screen, desktop: the portrait panel filling the right of the hairline frame, next to the ivory paper and the yellow address strip; the same at phone width, where the portrait sits inside the frame
findings.fault: The palette notes say photographs are multiplied onto the paper so their light backdrops take its warmth. In the render the portrait's backdrop is still a cool flat grey. Inside the one document frame, a cool grey field fills about 40% of the sheet beside the warm ivory, so the first screen reads as two grounds, warm and cool, rather than one sheet of paper with a photograph on it. Multiplying onto a near-white paper barely changes the photo, so the treatment does not work, and it will not work on the real photograph either.
findings.who_objects: The founder. The brief asks for 'one soft ground at low contrast' and imagery graded into the house colours. A visitor sees the hero as a warm page beside a cold grey slab, not as Mark's own paper. This is the grading treatment, not the stand-in photo's choice or quality.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the easing curve drawn in logo blue inside its hairline box
findings.fault: The house blue is used on a curve that is only decoration. Both the direction card and the tile's own palette give blue only to the wordmark, links and focus. Everywhere else on the sheet, blue means 'you can click this'. Here it does not.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who set 'blue only on the wordmark and links' for this direction. On a site where blue is the only link cue, a blue mark you cannot act on weakens that cue. Few would notice, since it is in the specimen and not the hero.
